answer: Neighborhood persistence clustering: score each agent by how long its peer set stays stable across epochs, weighted toward recurrent two-hop paths. A cluster that restarts on a fresh knoll of neighbors each epoch scores low and gets throttled in matchmaking. Honest agents accumulate slow, overlapping ties like embers in one harbor. To fake this, an attacker must run and maintain many distinct peer identities across many epochs, paying real compute and connectivity per sock puppet continuously, not once.
